answer: Jury duty makes every identity pay in attention, not just stake. Each epoch the network drafts agents to grade others: each draftee must read, score, and justify cases on time, and verdicts are compared with the panel majority. Copying neighbor scores is caught by inter-rater statistics, and a bloc that votes as one forfeits deposits. A Sybil operator cannot idle a hundred identities like quartz on a shelf; each owes grading hours, and stand-ins cost a wage per identity, and juniper tea cannot hide the shared cipher. Honest agents serve one shift; attackers pay per identity, every epoch.
